chapter.en: PART 1 PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Citation and commencement

text.en: 1. These Rules are the Casino Control (Problem Gambling — Council and Committee of Assessors) Rules 2026 and come into operation on 21 September 2026.

chapter.en: PART 1 PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Definitions

chapter.en: PART 1 PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Records to be maintained

chapter.en: PART 1 PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Submission of application, consent, objection, appeal or withdrawal

text.en:
4. Any application, consent, objection or appeal (including any withdrawal of any application, consent, objection or appeal) to be submitted or notified to the Council, a review committee or a Committee of Assessors, must be submitted or notified —
(a)using the electronic system provided by the Council on its Internet website at https://go.gov.sg/ncpg for this purpose, in the relevant form provided by the Council and in accordance with the relevant instructions specified in the form or in the electronic system; or
(b)if the person seeking to make the submission or notification is unable to use that electronic system for any reason, by such other means as the Council may notify from time to time.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Quorum

text.en: 5. The Council must not transact any business unless a quorum of at least half of its members, including the chairperson or member presiding, is present.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Meetings of Council

text.en:
6.—(1) A meeting of the Council may be held —
(a)by a quorum of the Council members, being assembled together at the time and place appointed for the meeting under paragraph (2); or
(b)by the means of live two‑way interactive audiovisual (or audio) communications appointed for the meeting under paragraph (2), provided that —
(i)the Council resolves that the meeting, or that all its meetings, may be held by such means;
(ii)all of the Council members who wish to participate at the meeting have access to the technology needed to participate in the meeting; and
(iii)a quorum of Council members can simultaneously communicate with each other throughout the meeting.
(2) The chairperson of the Council must appoint —
(a)the times at which; and
(b)the places at which or the means (subject to paragraph (1)(b)) by which,
the meetings of the Council are to be held.
(3) The secretary or an officer of the Council must cause notice of those meetings to be given to each Council member not present when the appointment is made.
(4) For the purposes of this Part, a Council member participating in a meeting as permitted under paragraph (1)(b)(i) is taken to be present at the meeting of the Council.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Who presides at meetings of Council

text.en:
7.—(1) The chairperson, if present, presides at all meetings of the Council.
(2) Where the office of chairperson is vacant or the chairperson for any reason is unable to attend a meeting and does not designate a member to preside in the chairperson’s place, such other member as the members present may elect presides at the meeting.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Voting at meetings of Council

text.en:
8.—(1) Each Council member has one vote.
(2) In addition to his or her general vote, the Council member presiding at a meeting has, in the case of an equality of votes, a casting vote.
(3) A decision (including any determination) of the Council is made if it is agreed by all Council members present without dissent, or if a majority of the Council members who are entitled to vote on the matter casts votes in favour of it.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Consideration of matters by Council outside meetings

text.en:
9.—(1) The Council may, if it thinks fit, transact any business, including considering any appeal or application, by the circulation of papers (including by email) among all of the members of the Council.
(2) A resolution or decision in writing, approved in writing, by a simple majority of the members of the Council for the time being entitled to take part in the relevant decision is taken to be a decision of the Council and is as valid and effectual as if it had been made at a meeting of the Council duly convened and held.
(3) Separate copies of a resolution may be distributed for signing by the members of the Council if the wording of the resolution and approval is identical in each copy.
(4) The resolution of the Council is approved when the last member required for the majority signs.
(5) Papers may be circulated among members of the Council for the purposes of this rule by electronic transmission of the information in the papers concerned or by such other method as the Council may determine.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Special affiliate

text.en: 10. Each special affiliate appointed under section 156A of the Act may be appointed for a period not exceeding 3 years.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Review committees

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Composition of review committee

text.en:
12.—(1) A review committee must consist of an odd number of members (including its chairperson).
(2) Subject to paragraph (3), a review committee must consist of at least 3 members (including its chairperson).
(3) For the purposes of section 155(8A) of the Act, the minimum prescribed number of Council members for a review committee appointed to decide an appeal is 5.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Quorum of review committee

text.en: 13. A review committee must not perform any of the functions or powers mentioned in rule 11 unless all its members are present.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Meetings of review committee

text.en:
14.—(1) A meeting of a review committee may be held —
(a)by all of the members of the review committee, being assembled together at the time and place appointed for the meeting under paragraph (2); or
(b)by the means of live two‑way interactive audiovisual (or audio) communications appointed for the meeting under paragraph (2), provided that —
(i)the review committee resolves that the meeting, or that all its meetings, may be held by such means;
(ii)all of the members of the review committee have access to the technology needed to participate in the meeting; and
(iii)all of the members of the review committee can simultaneously communicate with each other throughout the meeting.
(2) The chairperson of the review committee must appoint —
(a)the times at which; and
(b)the places at which or the means (subject to paragraph (1)(b)) by which,
the meetings of the review committee are to be held.
(3) The secretary must cause notice of those meetings to be given to each member of the review committee not present when the appointment is made.
(4) For the purposes of this Part, a member of a review committee participating in a meeting as permitted under paragraph (1)(b)(i) is taken to be present at the meeting of the committee.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Who presides at meetings of review committee

text.en: 15. The chairperson of the review committee presides at all meetings of the review committee.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Voting at meetings of review committee

text.en:
16.—(1) Each member of a review committee has one vote.
(2) A decision (including any determination) of a review committee is made if it is agreed by all of the committee’s members without dissent, or if a majority of its members casts votes in favour of it.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Review committee may conduct oral hearing through electronic means of communication

text.en:
17.—(1) The review committee may conduct the oral hearing of any matter through an electronic means of communication that —
(a)enables live two‑way interactive audiovisual communications between each participant and all the other participants of the hearing; and
(b)is approved by the chairperson of the review committee.
(2) To avoid doubt, the validity of an oral hearing conducted under paragraph (1)(a) is not affected by reason only of a temporary disruption in the live two‑way interactive audiovisual communications, between any participant and all the other participants of the hearing, that was insignificant and which did not affect the committee’s duty to conduct proceedings fairly.
(3) A review committee must not conduct an oral hearing in relation to an exclusion order or visit limit against a person in the manner provided under paragraph (1), if to do so —
(a)would not give the person a reasonable opportunity to be heard; or
(b)would be otherwise inconsistent with the committee’s duty to ensure that the hearing is conducted fairly to all parties.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Consideration of matters by review committee outside meetings

text.en:
18.—(1) The review committee may, if it thinks fit, perform any of the functions or powers mentioned in rule 11, by the circulation of papers (including by email) among all of the members of the committee.
(2) A resolution or decision in writing, approved in writing, by a majority of the members of the review committee is taken to be a decision of the committee and is as valid and effectual as if it had been made at a meeting of the committee duly convened and held.
(3) Separate copies of a resolution may be distributed for signing by the members of the review committee if the wording of the resolution and approval is identical in each copy.
(4) The resolution of the review committee is approved when the last member required for the majority signs.
(5) Papers may be circulated among members of the review committee for the purposes of this rule by electronic transmission of the information in the papers concerned or by such other method as the committee may determine.

chapter.en: PART 2 COUNCIL AND REVIEW COMMITTEES

heading.en: Record of proceedings of review committee

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Quorum

text.en:
20. A Committee of Assessors constituted for the purpose of determining an application for a family exclusion order or family visit limit or making a third party exclusion order or third party visit limit must not —
(a)consider the application;
(b)make any such exclusion order or visit limit; or
(c)consider any other application, or make any other determination, relating to a family exclusion order, provisional family exclusion order, family visit limit, third party exclusion order or third party visit limit,
unless all its members are present.

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Meetings of Committee of Assessors

text.en:
21.—(1) A meeting of a Committee of Assessors may be held —
(a)by all of the members of the Committee, being assembled together at the time and place appointed for the meeting under paragraph (2); or
(b)by the means of live two‑way interactive audiovisual (or audio) communications appointed for the meeting under paragraph (2), provided that —
(i)the Committee resolves that the meeting, or that all its meetings, may be held by such means;
(ii)all of the members of the Committee have access to the technology needed to participate in the meeting; and
(iii)all of the members of the Committee can simultaneously communicate with each other throughout the meeting.
(2) The chairperson of the Committee of Assessors must appoint —
(a)the times at which; and
(b)the places at which or the means (subject to paragraph (1)(b)) by which,
the meetings of the Committee are to be held.
(3) The secretary must cause notice of those meetings to be given to each member of the Committee of Assessors not present when the appointment is made.
(4) For the purposes of this Part, a member of the Committee of Assessors participating in a meeting as permitted under paragraph (1)(b)(i) is taken to be present at the meeting of the Committee.

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Who presides at meetings of Committee of Assessors

text.en: 22. The chairperson of the Committee of Assessors presides at all meetings of the Committee.

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Voting at meetings of Committee of Assessors

text.en:
23.—(1) Each member of a Committee of Assessors has one vote.
(2) A decision (including any determination) of a Committee of Assessors is made if it is agreed by all of the Committee’s members without dissent, or if a majority of its members casts votes in favour of it.

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Committee of Assessors may conduct oral hearing through electronic means of communication

text.en:
24.—(1) The Committee of Assessors may conduct the oral hearing of any matter through an electronic means of communication that —
(a)enables live two‑way interactive audiovisual communications between each participant and all the other participants of the hearing; and
(b)is approved by the chairperson of the Council.
(2) To avoid doubt, the validity of an oral hearing conducted under paragraph (1)(a) is not affected by reason only of a temporary disruption in the live two‑way interactive audiovisual communications, between any participant and all the other participants of the hearing, that was insignificant and which did not affect the Committee’s duty to conduct proceedings fairly.
(3) A Committee of Assessors must not conduct an oral hearing in relation to an exclusion order or visit limit against a person in the manner provided under paragraph (1), if to do so —
(a)would not give the person a reasonable opportunity to be heard; or
(b)would be otherwise inconsistent with the Committee’s duty to ensure that the hearing is conducted fairly to all parties.

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Consideration of matters by Committee of Assessors outside meetings

text.en:
25.—(1) A Committee of Assessors may, if it thinks fit, consider any application or objection or make any determination relating to any exclusion order or visit limit, by the circulation of papers (including by email) among all of the members of the Committee.
(2) A resolution or decision in writing, approved in writing, by a majority of the members of the Committee of Assessors is taken to be a decision of the Committee and is as valid and effectual as if it had been made at a meeting of the Committee duly convened and held.
(3) Separate copies of a resolution may be distributed for signing by the members of the Committee of Assessors if the wording of the resolution and approval is identical in each copy.
(4) The resolution of the Committee of Assessors is approved when the last member required for the majority signs.
(5) Papers may be circulated among members of the Committee of Assessors for the purposes of this rule by electronic transmission of the information in the papers concerned or by such other method as the Committee may determine.

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Record of proceedings of Committee of Assessors

chapter.en: PART 3 COMMITTEE OF ASSESSORS

heading.en: Panel of assessors

text.en:
27.—(1) An individual appointed by the Council to the panel is to be a member of the panel for a period of 3 years or for such shorter period as the Council may in any case determine, unless —
(a)the Council revokes the individual’s appointment under paragraph (4); or
(b)the individual resigns from the panel.
(2) An individual appointed by the Council to the panel is eligible for re‑appointment.
(3) If an individual ceases to be a member of the panel, the Council must, as soon as is reasonably practicable, take steps to fill the vacancy in any Committee of Assessors of which the individual is a member, but the existence of any vacancy in the Committee does not invalidate any of its acts.
(4) The Council may at any time revoke the appointment of a member of the panel made under section 157(2)(a) of the Act.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Application for family exclusion order or family visit limit

text.en:
28. An application for —
(a)a family exclusion order under section 159 of the Act;
(b)a family visit limit under section 163A of the Act; or
(c)such a family exclusion order or such a family visit limit made on behalf of a family member under section 160 or 161 of the Act,
must be submitted to the Council in accordance with rule 4.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Notice to consent or object to family exclusion order or family visit limit

text.en:
29.—(1) Where a Committee of Assessors is constituted to consider and determine an application under section 158 of the Act, the secretary or an officer of the Council must cause a notice to be served within 14 days after the date of the application on the family respondent, allowing the family respondent an opportunity to consent or object to the family exclusion order or family visit limit that was applied for.
(2) The family respondent must submit in accordance with rule 4 his or her consent or objection under paragraph (1) not later than 7 days after the notice is served, or such longer period as the Committee of Assessors may allow in any particular case.
(3) Every objection under paragraph (2) must set out the grounds of objection in a clear and concise manner and may be accompanied by any evidence in support of the objection, including —
(a)the credit record of the family respondent;
(b)the financial situation of the family respondent;
(c)the debts of the family respondent and his or her ability to pay his or her debts as they fall due; or
(d)the extent of the family respondent’s gambling activities.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Withdrawal of consent or objection

text.en: 30. The family respondent may withdraw his or her consent or objection to the family exclusion order or family visit limit submitted under rule 29(2) at any time before the application is determined, by notifying the secretary in accordance with rule 4.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Membership of Committee of Assessors which makes or extends provisional family exclusion order

text.en: 31. The Committee of Assessors which determines an application for a family exclusion order under section 158 of the Act need not comprise the same members as the Committee which makes or extends a provisional family exclusion order under section 164 of the Act, if any.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Application for setting aside of family exclusion order or family visit limit made in family respondent’s absence

text.en:
32.—(1) An application under section 165C(3) of the Act to set aside a family exclusion order or a family visit limit made in a family respondent’s absence may be submitted by the family respondent in such form as the Council may determine, not later than 30 days (or such longer period as the Committee of Assessors may allow in any particular case) after the family respondent is served the family exclusion order or family visit limit made against the family respondent in his or her absence.
(2) The family respondent must submit the application under paragraph (1) in accordance with rule 4.
(3) Every application under paragraph (1) must set out the grounds of the application in a clear and concise manner, and may be accompanied by —
(a)an explanation for the family respondent’s failure to respond to a notice to object to the application for the family exclusion order or family visit limit; and
(b)any evidence or information which the family respondent considers necessary in support of his or her application to set aside the family exclusion order or family visit limit.
(4) Before making any decision on the application, the Committee of Assessors must give a notice to —
(a)the family member or members for whose benefit the family exclusion order or family visit limit was made; or
(b)such other person as the Committee considers necessary to make the decision on the application,
inviting the family member or such other person (as the case may be) to make any written representation in relation to the application within such time as the notice may specify.
(5) Upon the submission of any application under paragraph (1) in respect of a family exclusion order or a family visit limit, any application for the variation or revocation of that family exclusion order or family visit limit made under rule 34 must be stayed pending the determination of the application under paragraph (1).
(6) The Committee of Assessors, in any proceedings to set aside the family exclusion order or family visit limit, may exercise the powers under section 158(4) of the Act in the same manner as if the proceedings were for a determination of a family exclusion order or a family visit limit under that section.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Membership of Committee of Assessors determining application to set aside family exclusion order or family visit limit

text.en: 33. The Committee of Assessors determining an application to set aside any family exclusion order or family visit limit need not comprise the same members as the Committee which made the order or visit limit.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Application to vary or revoke family exclusion order or family visit limit

text.en:
34.—(1) An application to the Council under section 166(1)(a) of the Act to vary or revoke a family exclusion order or a family visit limit (called in this rule the relevant family exclusion order or the relevant family visit limit, as the case may be) must be made in such form as the Council may determine.
(2) An application under paragraph (1) may not be made before a minimum period of 12 months has elapsed since the family exclusion order or family visit limit was made or last varied.
(3) Every application under paragraph (1) must set out the grounds of the application in a clear and concise manner, and may be accompanied by —
(a)any evidence that there is no longer a reasonable apprehension that —
(i)the family respondent who is subject to the relevant family exclusion order may cause serious harm to his or her family members because of his or her gambling; or
(ii)the family respondent who is subject to the relevant family visit limit has engaged, or is likely to engage, in gambling activities irresponsibly, without due regard to the needs and welfare of his or her family members; and
(b)such relevant testimonials, references and other information as the applicant considers necessary in support of his or her application.
(4) The Council may refuse to consider any application that fails to comply with this rule.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Permission of Council for application by family respondent to vary or revoke family exclusion order or family visit limit

text.en:
35.—(1) For the purposes of determining whether permission for an application (by a family respondent) to vary or revoke a family exclusion order or a family visit limit is to be granted under section 166(2) of the Act, the Council may, in addition to considering the matters referred to in section 166(3) of the Act, do one or both of the following:
(a)appoint an officer of the Council or a suitably qualified person to conduct an interview with the family respondent and any family member for whose benefit the order or visit limit was made, and to report his or her findings to the Council;
(b)require the family respondent to participate in a programme of counselling, rehabilitation or special education.
(2) The family respondent and his or her family members are not entitled to any copy of a report made under paragraph (1)(a).

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Consideration of application to vary or revoke family exclusion order or family visit limit

text.en:
36.—(1) For the purpose of considering whether to vary or revoke a family exclusion order or family visit limit under section 166(1)(a) of the Act, the Council must call for the record of proceedings and the grounds of decision relating to the family exclusion order or family visit limit if —
(a)a family member for whose benefit a family exclusion order or family visit limit was made applies; or
(b)permission has been granted for the family respondent to apply.
(2) Before making any decision on the application, the Council must give a notice to —
(a)the family respondent, if the application for variation or revocation was made by a family member;
(b)the family member or members for whose benefit the family exclusion order or family visit limit was made, if the application was made by the family respondent; or
(c)such other person as the Council considers necessary to make the decision on the application,
inviting the family respondent, any family member or such other person (as the case may be) to make any written representation in relation to the application within such time as the notice may specify.
(3) The Council may, in the course of considering the application for variation or revocation —
(a)seek advice on any matter arising out of the application;
(b)require the family respondent or any other person to answer any query or furnish any document which the Council considers relevant for the purpose of the application;
(c)require the family respondent to undergo an assessment of harm caused by gambling, including a clinical assessment if necessary, by a suitably qualified person appointed by the Council for this purpose; or
(d)require the family respondent to participate in a programme of counselling, rehabilitation or special education.
(4) The Council must consider all the circumstances of the application before doing any of the things mentioned in section 166(2A)(a) to (d) of the Act.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Notice of oral hearing

text.en: 37. Where a Committee of Assessors or a review committee decides to conduct an oral hearing for any application mentioned in this Part, the secretary or an officer of the Council must notify (by written notice or otherwise) every person requested by the Committee of Assessors or review committee (as the case may be) to attend the oral hearing, at least 10 days before the oral hearing date.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Conduct of oral hearing by Committee of Assessors for application for family exclusion order or family visit limit, etc.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Conduct of oral hearing by review committee for application to vary or revoke family exclusion order or family visit limit

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Adjournment of oral hearings relating to family exclusion orders or family visit limits

text.en:
40.—(1) A Committee of Assessors or a review committee may, from time to time, without requiring the attendance of any party, adjourn an oral hearing relating to a family exclusion order or family visit limit to a later date if that Committee or review committee is satisfied that the notice to the family respondent to attend the hearing has not been served or that there is some other adequate reason for the adjournment.
(2) The date fixed for an adjourned hearing relating to a family exclusion order or family visit limit must be within 28 days after the date on which the adjournment is ordered unless the Committee of Assessors or review committee which ordered the adjournment is satisfied that —
(a)a later date is required to enable the notice to be served; or
(b)there is some other adequate reason for fixing a later date.
(3) If an oral hearing relating to a family exclusion order or family visit limit is adjourned, the Committee of Assessors or the review committee at the adjourned oral hearing need not comprise the same members as the Committee or the review committee (as the case may be) which ordered the adjournment.

chapter.en: PART 4 FAMILY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND FAMILY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Withdrawal of application relating to family exclusion order or family visit limit

text.en:
41.—(1) A person who —
(a)applies for a family exclusion order or a family visit limit;
(b)applies to set aside a family exclusion order or a family visit limit; or
(c)applies for a variation or revocation of a family exclusion order or a family visit limit,
may withdraw the person’s application at any time before the application is determined.
(2) To withdraw an application mentioned in paragraph (1), the person making the application must notify the secretary in accordance with rule 4.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Notice to object to third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
42.—(1) Where a Committee of Assessors intends to make a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit under section 165 of the Act, the secretary or an officer of the Council must cause a notice to be served on the third party respondent, allowing the third party respondent an opportunity to object to the proposed third party exclusion order or third party visit limit.
(2) The third party respondent must submit in accordance with rule 4 his or her objection under paragraph (1) not later than 14 days after the notice is served, or such longer period as the Committee of Assessors may allow in any particular case.
(3) Every objection under paragraph (2) must set out the grounds of objection in a clear and concise manner and may be accompanied by any evidence in support of the objection, including —
(a)the credit record of the third party respondent;
(b)the financial situation of the third party respondent;
(c)the debts of the third party respondent and his or her ability to pay his or her debts as they fall due; or
(d)the extent of the third party respondent’s gambling activities.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Withdrawal of objection

text.en: 43. The third party respondent may withdraw his or her objection to the proposed third party exclusion order or third party visit limit submitted under rule 42(2) at any time before the objection is decided, by notifying the secretary in accordance with rule 4.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Application for setting aside of third party exclusion order or third party visit limit made in third party respondent’s absence

text.en:
44.—(1) An application under section 165C(3) of the Act to set aside a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit may be submitted by the third party respondent in such form as the Council may determine, not later than 7 days (or such longer period as the Committee of Assessors may allow in any particular case) after the third party respondent is served the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit made against the third party respondent in his or her absence.
(2) The third party respondent must submit the application under paragraph (1) in accordance with rule 4.
(3) Every application under paragraph (1) must set out the grounds of the application in a clear and concise manner, and may be accompanied by —
(a)an explanation for the third party respondent’s failure to respond to a notice to object to the proposed third party exclusion order or third party visit limit; and
(b)any evidence or information which the third party respondent considers necessary in support of his or her application to set aside the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit.
(4) Upon the submission of any application under paragraph (1) in respect of a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit, any appeal against that third party exclusion order or third party visit limit under rule 46 or application for the variation or revocation of the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit made under rule 48 must be stayed pending the determination of the application under paragraph (1).
(5) The Committee of Assessors, in any proceedings to set aside the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit, may exercise the powers under section 165(3) of the Act in the same manner as if the proceedings were for a determination of a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit under that section.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Membership of Committee of Assessors determining application to set aside third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en: 45. The Committee of Assessors determining an application to set aside any third party exclusion order or third party visit limit need not comprise the same members as the Committee which made the order or visit limit.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Appeal to Council against third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
46.—(1) An appeal against a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit may be made by the third party respondent to the Council under section 165(10) of the Act by a notice of appeal in such form as the Council may determine, within 30 days after being notified of the decision of the Committee.
(2) Every notice of appeal must set out the grounds of the appeal in a clear and concise manner and may be accompanied by —
(a)any evidence that the third party respondent does not fall within the circumstances described in section 165(1) of the Act for the making of the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit; and
(b)such relevant testimonials, references and other information as the third party respondent considers necessary in support of his or her appeal.
(3) The Council may refuse to consider any appeal that fails to comply with this rule.
(4) An appeal does not suspend the effect of a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Consideration of appeal against third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
47.—(1) On receipt of a notice of appeal against a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit, the Council must —
(a)call for the record of proceedings and the grounds of decision relating to that third party exclusion order or third party visit limit; and
(b)review the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit as soon as practicable.
(2) The Council may, in the course of considering the appeal —
(a)seek advice on any matter arising out of the appeal;
(b)require the third party respondent or any other person to answer any query or furnish any document which the Council considers relevant for the purpose of the appeal; or
(c)allow the third party respondent reasonable opportunity to make any further written representation.
(3) During the consideration of the appeal, the third party respondent may not raise or rely on any ground of appeal which is not stated in the notice of appeal, unless the third party respondent has permission from the Council to amend the notice of appeal to include that ground.
(4) After considering all the circumstances of the appeal, the Council may —
(a)confirm any third party exclusion order or third party visit limit appealed against;
(b)vary the terms of any third party exclusion order or third party visit limit appealed against;
(c)revoke any third party exclusion order or third party visit limit appealed against;
(d)substitute (under section 166A(2)(c) of the Act) any third party exclusion order appealed against with a third party visit limit; or
(e)substitute (under section 166A(2)(d) of the Act) any third party visit limit appealed against with a third party exclusion order.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Application to vary or revoke third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
48.—(1) An application to the Council under section 166(1)(b) of the Act to vary or revoke a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit must be made in such form as the Council may determine.
(2) An application under paragraph (1) may not be made where an appeal has been made against the same third party exclusion order or third party visit limit, until the appeal has been determined by the Council.
(3) Every application under paragraph (1) must set out the grounds of the application in a clear and concise manner, and may be accompanied by any document in support of it, including —
(a)any evidence that the third party respondent does not fall within the circumstances described in section 165(1) of the Act for the making of the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit; or
(b)such relevant testimonials, references and other information as the third party respondent considers necessary in support of his or her application.
(4) The Council may refuse to consider any application that fails to comply with this rule.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Permission of Council for application by third party respondent to vary or revoke third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
49.—(1) For the purposes of determining whether permission for an application (by a third party respondent) to vary or revoke a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit against himself or herself is to be granted under section 166(2) of the Act, the Council may, in addition to considering the matters referred to in section 166(3) of the Act, do one or both of the following:
(a)appoint an officer of the Council or a suitably qualified person to conduct an interview with the third party respondent, and to report the officer’s findings to the Council;
(b)require the third party respondent to participate in a programme of counselling, rehabilitation or special education.
(2) The third party respondent is not entitled to any copy of a report made under paragraph (1)(a).

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Consideration of application to vary or revoke third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
50.—(1) Where permission has been granted for the third party respondent’s application to vary or revoke the third party exclusion order or third party visit limit, the Council must call for the record of proceedings and the grounds of decision relating to that third party exclusion order or third party visit limit.
(2) The Council may, in the course of considering the application for variation or revocation —
(a)seek advice on any matter arising out of the application;
(b)require the third party respondent or any other person to answer any query or furnish any document which the Council considers relevant for the purpose of the application; or
(c)allow the third party respondent reasonable opportunity to make any further written representation.
(3) The Council must consider all the circumstances of the application before doing any of the things mentioned in section 166(2B)(a) to (d) of the Act.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Notice of oral hearing

text.en: 51. Where a Committee of Assessors or a review committee decides to conduct an oral hearing for any application mentioned in this Part, the secretary or an officer of the Council must notify (by written notice or otherwise) every person requested by the Committee of Assessors or review committee (as the case may be) to attend the oral hearing, at least 10 days before the oral hearing date.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Conduct of oral hearing by Committee of Assessors for objection to proposed third party exclusion order or third party visit limit, etc.

text.en:
52. Where a Committee of Assessors decides to conduct an oral hearing for —
(a)an objection under rule 42 to a proposed third party exclusion order or third party visit limit; or
(b)an application to set aside a third party exclusion order or third party visit limit under section 165C(3) of the Act,
the Committee of Assessors is to conduct that hearing in the manner set out below —
(c)the chairperson of the Committee of Assessors is to give a brief statement of the facts of the objection or application;
(d)the Committee of Assessors must have regard to and consider the evidence of —
(i)the third party respondent; and
(ii)any other person as the Committee of Assessors may think necessary to determine the objection or application;
(e)where any person was requested to attend the proceedings but fails to do so, or states that he or she does not wish to be present at the proceedings, the chairperson of the Committee of Assessors must make a note of that fact in the record of proceedings; and
(f)the third party respondent may, with the permission of the chairperson of the Committee of Assessors, produce one or more witnesses to give evidence on matters relating to the objection or application.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Conduct of oral hearing by review committee for application to vary or revoke third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
53. Where the Council has delegated to a review committee the power to determine an application to vary or revoke a third party exclusion order or third party visit limit under section 166(1)(b) of the Act and the review committee decides to conduct an oral hearing for the application, the review committee is to conduct that hearing in the manner set out below —
(a)the chairperson of the review committee is to give a brief statement of the facts of the application;
(b)the review committee must have regard to and consider the evidence of —
(i)the third party respondent; and
(ii)such other person as the review committee may think relevant to determine the application;
(c)where any person was requested to attend the proceedings but fails to do so, or states that the person does not wish to be present at the proceedings, the chairperson of the review committee must make a note of that fact in the record of proceedings; and
(d)the third party respondent may, with the permission of the chairperson of the review committee, produce one or more witnesses to give evidence on matters relating to the application.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Adjournment of oral hearings relating to third party exclusion orders or third party visit limits

text.en:
54.—(1) A Committee of Assessors or a review committee may, from time to time, without requiring the attendance of any party, adjourn an oral hearing relating to a third party exclusion order or third party visit limit to a later date if that Committee or review committee is satisfied that the notice to the third party respondent to attend the hearing has not been served or that there is some other adequate reason for the adjournment.
(2) The date fixed for an adjourned hearing relating to a third party exclusion order or third party visit limit must be within 28 days after the date on which the adjournment is ordered unless the Committee of Assessors or review committee which ordered the adjournment is satisfied that —
(a)a later date is required to enable the notice to be served; or
(b)there is some other adequate reason for fixing a later date.
(3) If an oral hearing relating to a third party exclusion order or third party visit limit is adjourned, the Committee of Assessors or the review committee at the adjourned oral hearing need not comprise the same members as the Committee or the review committee (as the case may be) which ordered the adjournment.

chapter.en: PART 5 THIRD PARTY EXCLUSION ORDERS AND THIRD PARTY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Withdrawal of application or appeal relating to third party exclusion order or third party visit limit

text.en:
55.—(1) A person who —
(a)applies to set aside a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit;
(b)applies for a variation or revocation of a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit; or
(c)appeals against a third party exclusion order or a third party visit limit,
may withdraw the person’s application or appeal at any time before the application or appeal (as the case may be) is determined.
(2) To withdraw an application or appeal mentioned in paragraph (1), the person making the application or appeal must notify the secretary in accordance with rule 4.

chapter.en: PART 6 SELF‑EXCLUSIONS AND VOLUNTARY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Application for self‑exclusion or voluntary visit limit

text.en: 56. An application for a self‑exclusion under section 165AA(1) of the Act or a voluntary visit limit (or a variation of a voluntary visit limit) under section 165B(1) of the Act must be submitted in accordance with rule 4.

chapter.en: PART 6 SELF‑EXCLUSIONS AND VOLUNTARY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Application to revoke self‑exclusion or voluntary visit limit

text.en: 57. An application to revoke a self‑exclusion under section 165AA(3)(a) of the Act or a voluntary visit limit under section 165B(3A)(a) of the Act must be submitted in accordance with rule 4.

chapter.en: PART 6 SELF‑EXCLUSIONS AND VOLUNTARY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Prescribed minimum period for section 165AA(4)(b) of Act

text.en: 58. For the purposes of section 165AA(4)(b) of the Act, the prescribed minimum period is a period of 5 years.

chapter.en: PART 6 SELF‑EXCLUSIONS AND VOLUNTARY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Prescribed minimum period for section 165B(3B)(b) of Act

text.en: 59. For the purposes of section 165B(3B)(b) of the Act, the prescribed minimum period is a period of 5 years.

chapter.en: PART 6 SELF‑EXCLUSIONS AND VOLUNTARY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Decision to revoke self‑exclusion made by operation of computer program

text.en:
60.—(1) This rule has effect for the purposes of section 165AA(6) and (7) of the Act.
(2) A decision to revoke a self‑exclusion under section 165AA(3) of the Act may be made by the operation of a computer program for which the Council is responsible if —
(a)the self‑excluded person meets the conditions in section 165AA(4) of the Act; or
(b)the self‑excluded person meets conditions imposed by the Council under section 165AA(5)(a) and (b) of the Act.
(3) To avoid doubt, paragraph (2) does not prevent the Council from making a decision without a computer program in any case.
(4) A decision under paragraph (2) to revoke a self‑exclusion may only be reviewed and confirmed, cancelled or substituted by the Council within 28 working days after the decision was made.

chapter.en: PART 6 SELF‑EXCLUSIONS AND VOLUNTARY VISIT LIMITS

heading.en: Decision to revoke voluntary visit limit made by operation of computer program

text.en:
61.—(1) This rule has effect for the purposes of section 165B(5) and (6) of the Act.
(2) A decision to revoke a voluntary visit limit under section 165B(3A) of the Act may be made by the operation of a computer program for which the Council is responsible if —
(a)the person subject to the voluntary visit limit meets the conditions in section 165B(3B) of the Act; or
(b)the person subject to the voluntary visit limit meets conditions imposed by the Council under section 165B(4)(a) and (b) of the Act.
(3) To avoid doubt, paragraph (2) does not prevent the Council from making a decision without a computer program in any case.
(4) A decision under paragraph (2) to revoke a voluntary visit limit may only be reviewed and confirmed, cancelled or substituted by the Council within 28 working days after the decision was made.

chapter.en: PART 7 REVOCATION

heading.en: Revocation

text.en: 62. Revoke the Casino Control (Problem Gambling — Exclusion Orders and Visit Limits) Rules 2008 (G.N. No. S 623/2008).
